neon.tip: Cardinal and green neon have different red patterns from the true neon. Cardinal: the red stripe runs the whole length of the belly, from the gills to the tail. Neon: the red covers only the rear half of the body. Green neon: much smaller, with a short red patch near the tail.

rummy.tip: True rummy-nose (Hemigrammus): red on the nose only, with clean black-and-white tail bars. Brilliant/false rummy (Petitella): the red covers more of the head and the tail bars are bolder.

bigtetra.tip: Congo: big scales with a rainbow sheen, males have flowing fins. Emperor: dark stripe along the body, with a longer extended tail middle. Buenos Aires and black skirt tetras are deeper-bodied with dark bands.

skirt.tip: Black skirt: wide black fade at the rear and tall fins. Serpae: red-orange body with a black shoulder spot. Bleeding heart: a single red spot behind the gill on a pink body.

redbarb.tip: Rosy: copper-pink body with a black tail base spot in males that glow rosy red. Cherry: red body with a dark stripe through the eye. Tiger: four black vertical bars with orange-red fins; albino is pale gold and green has a deep green sheen. Odessa: red stripe along the middle of the body. Gold and checkerboard: golden or spotted.

algae.tip: Siamese algae eater: a clean black stripe from the nose through the eye all the way to the end of the tail. Flying fox: a gold stripe above the black one, and the stripe stops at the tail base. Chinese algae eater: golden, larger sucker mouth and a blotchy stripe, grows big and aggressive.

cory.tip: Skunk: black stripe along the back with an orange tint. Panda: black eye patches, black tail base and dorsal spot. Bronze/Aeneus: plain metallic bronze or green. Albino: pale pink with red eyes. Julii: spotted head with lines. Three-stripe: three dark stripes along the side; very similar to julii. Arched: a black stripe arching from the eye over the back. Rabauti: a dark stripe along the body, orange tint on the sides. Black Venezuela: dark with a gold tint. Orange laser: a bright orange stripe along the back. Peppered: dark pepper spots over gray. Sterbai: dark with orange pectoral fins. Pygmy: under 1 inch, swims mid-water. Emerald (Brochis): longer-bodied and bigger than a bronze, with a bright metallic green-blue sheen and a taller dorsal fin.

loach.tip: Kuhli: thin eel-like with dark and tan bands. Clown: orange with black bands and red fins. Yoyo: marks that read "Y-O-Y-O" along the body. Zebra: pale with dark vertical stripes. Dojo/weather loach: long, plain, whiskered. Hillstream: flat, clings to glass.

rainbow.tip: Boesemani: front half blue-gray, back half orange-yellow. Turquoise: blue-green overall. Australian/splendid: stripe along the side with orange fins. Dwarf neon: under 2 inches with a red-stripe fade. Red: all red males. Threadfin: very tall twin dorsal fins.

guppy.tip: Endler: under an inch and a half, bright pattern, small tail. Guppy: larger, big fan-like tail in many colors. Platy: stockier with a rounded tail. Red wag platy: red body with black fins. Mickey Mouse platy: three black dots at the tail base. Sunburst platy: orange-yellow body. Swordtail: males have a long sword on the tail; green, red and pineapple are color forms. Molly: larger and taller with a big dorsal fin; black molly is solid black, sailfin has a tall sail-like dorsal, dalmatian is white with black spots, balloon has a round belly and bent spine. Variatus platy: slimmer and more angular than a common platy. Least killifish: tiny, mosquitofish-like.

danio.tip: Zebra: horizontal blue-white stripes. Pearl: pearly sheen with a pink stripe. Leopard: spots instead of stripes. White cloud: tiny with a red tail base and a gold stripe. Celestial pearl danio: tiny with pale spots on dark blue.

rasbora.tip: Harlequin: copper body with a black triangle. Lambchop: thinner, longer black wedge. Espei: red-orange with a black wedge that starts at the middle. Chili: tiny and bright red. Scissortail: black-and-white striped tail.

gourami.tip: Dwarf: small, blue and red vertical stripes over the body, with thread-like pelvic fins. Powder blue is pale blue, neon blue is bright electric blue, flame is red-orange: all color forms of the dwarf. Honey: smaller and plain, yellow-orange to tan. Pearl: pearly spots with a dark line from nose to tail. Three-spot: larger, with a spot mid-body and one at the tail base. Blue is blue-gray, gold is yellow, opaline is marbled blue: all color forms of the three-spot. Kissing: pink, with big lips. Banded: striped, with a spiny dorsal fin.

pleco.tip: Bristlenose: fleshy tentacles on the snout; albino is pale pink, longfin has flowing fins. Common: very large with a sail-like dorsal fin. Clown pleco: small with orange bands. Zebra pleco: small, bold black-and-white stripes. Blue phantom: dark blue-gray with light spots. Leopard frog: leopard-like spots on a light body. Candy stripe: fine light stripes on dark. Bulldog: flat, with a wide, rounded sucker mouth. Otocinclus: tiny with a dark stripe, a flat sucker.

stick.tip: Twig catfish (Farlowella): very thin like a twig, with a long pointed snout. Whiptail (Rineloricaria): flatter body with a long thin whip-like tail.

cichmal.tip: Yellow lab: bright yellow with a black dorsal edge. Red zebra: orange to peach with a blotchy pattern. Cobalt zebra: blue with dark bars. Demasoni: small, blue with thick black bars. Kenyi: males yellow-orange, females blue bars. Peacocks: brilliant solid colors, long pointed body.

cichsa.tip: Angelfish: tall with long trailing fins; marble is black and white, koi has orange patches, zebra has dark stripes, veil has very long fins, black is nearly solid black. Oscar: large, orange-patterned dark body and a tail spot; albino is pale, red is solid red-orange. Convict: black and white vertical stripes. Jack Dempsey: dark with bright blue-green flecks; electric blue is a bright blue form. Severum: round, with a faint orange or gold tint; gold is pale gold and red spotted has red-orange spots. Blue acara: gray-blue with a vertical dark bar behind the gill and blue speckles. Firemouth: red throat and belly. Keyhole: tiny with a keyhole-shaped spot.

dwarfcich.tip: German blue ram: blue-yellow with a black spot behind the head and red fins. Bolivian ram: duller, with a stripe over the eye. Kribensis (Pelvicachromis): elongated body, a purple-pink belly in females, a dark stripe along the side and eye-spots in the tail. Apistogramma: small with a rounded tail, males show a dark horizontal stripe and a frilled dorsal.

tanganyika.tip: Julidochromis: elongated with black stripes. Princess (brichardi): elegant, with extended fins and a light blue edge. Shell dwellers: tiny, rest in shells. Cyprichromis: slender, free-swimming and in schools.

puffer.tip: Pea puffer: tiny yellow-green with brown spots. Figure-8: rounder, with a figure-8 pattern on its back. Both are small, rounded and slow-moving.

betta.tip: Halfmoon: tail opens a full 180 degrees, very full fins. Crowntail: spiky fin rays with webbing pulled back. Veiltail: long drooping tail that hangs down. Plakat: short, rounded fins and a sturdier body. Dragon scale: thick, metallic scales on the body. Female bettas have short fins and a pale egg spot. Paradise fish: striped red and blue with a forked tail. Wild bettas are small and dull, with short fins.

goldfish.tip: Common/comet: long, slim body with a single tail (comet has a long forked tail). Fantail: short egg-shaped body, double tail. Ryukin: tall hump behind the head, double tail. Veiltail: very long flowing double tail. Ranchu/Lionhead: no back fin and a head hood; ranchu has a curved back and a short tail, lionhead a flatter back. Oranda: back fin and a head hood. Pompom: fleshy pompoms by the nostrils. Celestial/telescope/bubble eye: unusual eyes. Pearlscale: round with raised scales. Shubunkin: calico pattern, single tail. Koi: barbels and a wide range of colors.

shrimpf.tip: Cherry: bright red (Neocaridina). Crystal red and bee shrimp: bands of white with red or black, with a clear-white body. Rili: a cherry shrimp variety, red with large clear patches. Tiger: thin stripes with orange eyes. Blue bolt: blue bands. Amano: gray-clear with dotted lateral spots. Ghost/glass: fully transparent. Bamboo/wood: large and brown, with fan arms. Blue velvet: solid blue.

nerite.tip: Zebra nerite: black stripes on gold. Tiger nerite: bold dark stripes. Horned nerite: has little horns. Olive nerite: plain, with a speckled olive shell. Mystery/apple snail: large, round, smooth shell in gold, blue or ivory.

cfish.tip: Ocellaris: orange with three white bands and thin black edging. Percula: thicker black edging between bands and a more rounded body. Percula and ocellaris are very hard to tell apart from a photo; percula has 10 dorsal spines and ocellaris has 11. Maroon: dark red with a single bright stripe. Clarkii: darker body with a yellow tail. Tomato: bright red-orange, with a single patch behind the eye.

tang.tip: Yellow: all bright yellow. Regal/hippo: blue with a black palette shape and yellow tail. Atlantic blue: plain blue-gray, yellow when young, no palette. Purple: purple with a yellow tail. Red Sea sailfin: tall sail with vertical white bars on a dark body. Pacific sailfin: tall sail, olive-brown with pale bars. Scopas: brown with a pale tail base. Kole: dark with a gold ring around the eye. Chocolate: brown with a pale face. Goldrim: dark with a white cheek and a gold rim on the tail. Sohal: striped blue-gray with an orange spot by the tail spine. Powder blue: sky blue with a white face and yellow dorsal. Naso types: a long horn or slim body with no dorsal sail. Vlamingi: very large with a bulging forehead.

damsel.tip: Blue-green chromis: bright blue-green, shoals in groups. Yellowtail damsel: royal blue with a yellow tail. Domino: black with white spots. Three-stripe: white with three black bars. Azure: blue and yellow. Talbot's: yellow back and blue front. Springer's: deep blue with a bright blue face.

gobyb.tip: Firefish: white nose and a red tail with a long dorsal spike. Yellow watchman: yellow body with a long dorsal fin. Lawnmower blenny: brown with a sloped face. Tailspot blenny: spotted with a stripe on the tail. Bicolor blenny: two-tone, with a dark head and yellow tail.

mandarin.tip: Mandarin: orange, blue and green swirls, slow along the rock. Psychedelic mandarin: the same but with a more intense maze-like pattern.

wrasse.tip: Six-line wrasse: six stripes. Melanurus: a black tail spot. Fairy wrasses: bright with long fins; exquisite has blue-green sides, Lubbock's is orange and purple, Scott's has bold bars. Cleaner wrasse: thin blue stripe. Moon wrasse: green to blue-green body (looks blue under reef lights), pink or orange bands on the head, and a bright yellow crescent tail. Yellowtail tamarin: as sold, dark brown to black covered in small white spots, with a yellow tail; never blue-green. Purple queen anthias: purple with gold, in groups. Lyretail anthias: orange with long, lyre-shaped tail points.

angel.tip: Flame angel: red-orange with vertical dark bars. Coral beauty: blue to orange with a dark shoulder. Bicolor: the front half is deep blue-purple and the back half is bright yellow, and it stays small. Half black: pale front, black rear half. Flameback: dark body with an orange back. Rock beauty: yellow with a large black patch over the back and tail. Lemonpeel: all yellow with a blue ring around the eye. Keyhole: dark with a pale tail and a white keyhole mark. Multicolor: a rainbow of orange, blue and yellow. Blueface and majestic: large angelfish; blueface has a blue face and yellow body, majestic is dark with blue edges and yellow lines. Butterflyfish: copperband has a long snout with a copper stripe; longnose is yellow with a very long snout; pyramid is yellow and white; Klein's is brown-yellow with an eye stripe; raccoon has a black mask.

euph.tip: Hammer: heads with hammer-shaped or anchor tentacle tips. Frogspawn: branching tentacle tips like frog eggs. Torch: long single-tipped tentacles. Duncan: short, round, fleshy polyps with a visible white stony skeleton below them, in a branching bush; not a plating coral. Torch: long fleshy tentacles with rounded tips on a branching skeleton. A carpet anemone is a different animal: one wide, flat disc with short sticky tentacles and no branching skeleton.

softc.tip: Xenia: pulsing, waving stalks. Green star polyps: bright green mats with small arms. Kenya tree: a tree-like stalk branching into small heads. Leather (toadstool): wide, thick cap that folds in. Clove polyps: dense stalks with pale tips.

zoa.tip: Zoanthid/palythoa: groups of small round polyps in colonies and mats. Mushrooms (Discosoma): single smooth, flat discs with a slit mouth in the middle, no tentacles and no stalk. Ricordea: flatter bumpy disks. Rhodactis: larger and hairy-looking.

sps.tip: Acropora: branching with a tip polyp. Montipora: plating or encrusting with tiny polyps. Birdsnest/Seriatopora: thin fine branches. Stylophora: thick branches. Porites: smooth, stony fingers or plates with tiny round polyps. Cauliflower (Pocillopora): thick, bumpy branches with small wart-like bumps (verrucae) and no leafy plates. Pavona: leafy, layered plates. Montipora has no tip polyp, and its surface is covered in tiny rough pores.

lps.tip: Brain (Lobophyllia/Favia): round or dome-shaped with ridged, maze-like valleys. Trachyphyllia: flat and folded. Goniopora: long flowerpot-like polyps, delicate. Bubble coral: bubbly sacs. Candy cane: each polyp on its own stalk. Galaxea: clumps of long, hairy-looking sweeper tentacles on round polyps with a sharp stony wall. Cynarina/Scolymia: one big fleshy polyp with no tentacles.

anemone.tip: Bubble-tip: bulb tips on tentacles. Long tentacle: long flowing tentacles and a bigger body. Carpet: flat, wide, sticky tentacles. Condy: long, thin tentacles with pink tips. Aiptasia: tiny glassy pest.

crab.tip: Blue-leg hermit: blue legs with orange bands. Red-leg hermit: red legs. Emerald crab: green, mostly stationary. Sally Lightfoot: bright red and orange, runs fast.

reefsnail.tip: Turbo: large and round, with a rough shell. Nassarius: small cones that burrow. Astraea: flat coin-like shell. Cerith: thin spiral.

sword.tip: Amazon sword (Echinodorus): large, wide, rigid leaves with a clear midrib, held on stiff stalks and growing from one thick crown. Narrow-leaf swords: thinner leaves. Often large and stand in the middle or back of the tank. Not a sword: Aponogeton has thin, wavy, softer leaves from a bulb (madagascar lace has holes); Bacopa has small paired leaves along a stem.

crypt.tip: Crypts form a rosette with crinkled leaves. Wendtii: wavy leaves in green to bronze. Parva: tiny and compact. Balansae: long, strap-like leaves.

val.tip: Vallisneria: long, thin ribbon leaves. Sagittaria: grass-like blades on a base, usually shorter. Jungle val: giant and broad. Madagascar lace plant (Aponogeton) is not a val: its leaves are a netted lattice with holes, like lace. Pygmy chain sword: short grass-like blades.

stem.tip: Ludwigia: oval leaves in pairs on a stem, red underside. Rotala: tiny narrow leaves in whorls, pink to red tips. Bacopa: thick round leaves. Hygrophila: pointy, often broad leaves. Alternanthera: red or maroon leaves. Hornwort looks feathery, with stiff whorls of thin forked needle-like leaves on a stem and no roots. Only call a plant Hornwort if the leaves are needle-like, not flat.

fern.tip: Java fern: finger-like fronds, small black spots under leaves. Anubias: thick dark arrowhead leaves. Mosses: green fuzzy mats on wood or rocks. Bolbitis: wavy dark fronds. Fissidens: tiny flat fern-like leaves in two neat rows, like little feathers. Flame moss: fine upright, flame-shaped growth with thin stringy stems.

float.tip: Frogbit: small round leaves with roots hanging down. Water lettuce: rosettes like tiny cabbages. Salvinia: round, hairy leaves. Duckweed: tiny dots covering the surface.

carpet.tip: Dwarf hairgrass: very fine grass-like carpet. Monte Carlo: rounded tiny leaves. Dwarf baby tears: tiny round leaves in a dense mat. Glosso: tiny paddle leaves.

macro.tip: Chaeto: fuzzy green balls or strands. Caulerpa: grape-like or feathery green runners. Halimeda: segmented, stiff.

geo.tip: Eartheaters have a sloped head, a downturned mouth and sift sand. Red-head types have a red-orange head; striped types have a dark band and spot. Many species look alike in stores, so the exact species is hard to tell from a photo.

cichca.tip: Texas: pearl-spotted, stocky and gray-blue. Jaguar: long with a big mouth and dark blotches. Midas and red devil: orange or gold with a nuchal hump. Salvini: yellow with a dark stripe. Rainbow cichlid: smaller with a gold body and dark stripes. Blood parrot: round orange hybrid with a beak-like mouth. Flowerhorn: a hybrid with a large forehead bump.

discus.tip: Heckel: round body with a dark central bar and reddish-brown color. Blue diamond: solid blue with little striping. Pigeon blood: cream with orange and pink patches. Red turquoise: red with blue-green stripes. Snakeskin: net-like pattern across the body. Albino: pale with red eyes. Most discus sold are strains of the same fish, so color alone is not a reliable guide.

tetra.tip: Black neon: neon-like with a white stripe over a black stripe. Lemon: pale yellow with a glowing red eye. Glowlight: orange stripe along the middle. Ember: small, solid orange-red. Rosy: pink and silver with a dark dorsal edge. Diamond: shiny scales with a long dorsal fin. Gold: golden yellow. Penguin: dark stripe along the body. Bloodfin: silver with red fins. X-ray: nearly see-through with a pale stripe. Splash: a white tail spot and a stripe on the body. Silvertip: silver with white fin tips. Blue: pale blue with a long dorsal fin. Ruby: tiny, red. Colombian: red-orange fins on a dark body.

hatchet.tip: Marbled: marbled brown pattern with a deep keel, about 1.5 inches. Silver: plain silver with a flatter, longer body, up to about 2.5 inches. Both swim at the surface and have a very deep chest.

pencil.tip: Golden (Beckford's): a gold stripe edged in black. Three-lined: three dark stripes along the side. Coral red: red tail and fins with a dark body. Dwarf: a short, slim body with a red tail spot. All hold their body at a slant.

shark.tip: Rainbow shark: dark body with red fins; albino has a pale body with red fins. Red-tailed black shark: black body with a bright red tail. Iridescent shark: silver-gray catfish with a long forked tail, very large. Columbian shark: silver with black fin edges. Bala shark: silver with black-edged fins. Glofish shark is a dyed or modified rainbow shark.

cat.tip: Pictus: silver with black spots and very long whiskers. Synodontis: large with a mottled or spotted body; upside-down types swim belly-up. Raphael: dark with a white stripe along the side. Bumblebee: yellow and black bands. Glass: see-through. Banjo: flat, like a leaf. Hoplo: armored with a row of plates. Featherfin: a dark spotted pattern with a large, fan-like dorsal fin.

trigger.tip: Niger: dark, with a pale line along the cheek. Picasso: bold mask and abstract black, yellow and blue patterns. Pinktail: dark body with a pink tail. Clown: large white spots on a dark underside and yellow face. Bluethroat: blue-green throat and yellow-edged fins.

dotty.tip: Royal gramma: purple front half and yellow back half. Royal dottyback: purple with a dark stripe through the eye. Strawberry dottyback: bright magenta. Sunrise dottyback: yellow-orange with a dark stripe. Orchid dottyback: purple with a bright yellow line. Dottybacks are more aggressive than grammas.

hawk.tip: Flame: red-orange face and body with a dark stripe through the eye. Falco: red cross-hatch pattern with a dark eye stripe. Longnose: long, pointed face and a checked pattern. Pixy: small, with a spotted body and stripes through the eye. All perch on rocks.

seahorse.tip: Lined: dark lines across the neck and body. Yellow (kuda): smooth, plain yellow or orange body. Pipefish: long and straight, without a curled tail. Dragonface pipefish: straight body with a pointed, dragon-like face.

bichir.tip: Ornate: dark stripes along a pale body, with a spotted or banded look. Senegal: olive-gray with a lighter underside. Reedfish: long and snake-like.

lion.tip: Volitans: large, red-and-white banded, with long feathery pectoral fins. Radiata: smaller, with white-edged fins and bars. Spotfin: thin lines, spots on the fins and a longer, finer look. Dwarf zebra: small, with a short, stocky body. All have venomous spines.

c.n: Easy, colorful LPS that likes to be fed. Low to medium light, low to medium flow.
One of the milder mbuna, silvery blue with a yellow tail. Likes rocks and can live with other peaceful Malawi cichlids.
Beautiful but difficult tang with an orange spot at the tail base. Needs a large tank, strong flow and very clean water.
Branching SPS that needs very stable, clean water and strong light and flow. For experienced keepers.
Elegant cory with an orange patch on the head. Needs a school, sand and clean water.
Mbuna with a blue body and a white or yellow top. Territorial. Keep in a crowded rocky tank.
Small, peaceful cichlid with a butterfly pattern. Good in a community tank with other peaceful fish.
Surface fish with wing-like fins that jumps and eats small fish. Needs a tight lid.
Colorful dwarf cichlid in many color forms. Keep one male with several females in a planted tank with caves.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, micro pellets

c.n: Electric blue males, a close cousin of the Electric Blue Hap. Peaceful with similar-sized fish.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen mysis, brine shrimp

c.n: A pest anemone that spreads fast and stings corals. Peppermint shrimp and copperband butterflies eat it.
Pale pink bristlenose with red eyes. Same care as other bristlenose: eats algae and wood, needs driftwood and hiding spots.
Pale pink version of the bronze cory. Hardy, social and best kept in groups.
Pale discus with red eyes and little dark pigment. Sensitive and needs warm, soft, very clean water. Keep in a group.
c.f: Discus pellets, frozen bloodworms, beef heart

c.n: Pale oscar with red eyes and orange-yellow patterns. Big, smart and messy. Eats any fish that fits in its mouth.
Pale gold tiger barb with orange-red fins and pink eyes. Bold fin-nippers, so keep eight or more and avoid long-finned tankmates.
Two-band clownfish from East Africa, close to the clarkii. Hardy and bold; keep a single pair.
Maroon-red stem plant that needs strong light and iron. Looks great in a planted tank.
Tall, delicate angelfish that needs warm, soft, acidic, very clean water. Not a beginner fish.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Delicate cousin of Goniopora with longer, thinner polyps. Needs stable water and regular feeding. Not for beginners.
Larger, excellent algae eaters. Tough and clean-minded, though larvae need brackish water to grow.
Floating plant with long, trailing roots. Shades the tank and soaks up nutrients; useful for shy fish.
Ambush hunter that looks like a dead leaf. Eats any fish that fits in its mouth, so keep it alone or with larger tankmates.
c.f: Live or frozen small fish and shrimp

c.n: Big, hardy background plant with broad leaves. Heavy root feeder, so use root tabs.
Fast, feathery stem plant that soaks up nutrients and shades out algae. Trim often. Easy for beginners.
Delicate stem plant with a red tint under bright light. Needs steady nutrients and CO2 to look its best.
Fast, easy stem plant that soaks up nutrients. Float it or plant it.
Fine-branched SPS, a bit easier than acropora. Strong light and good flow.
Tall, elegant cichlid that needs a tall tank. Adults may eat very small fish like neons; pairs defend breeding spots.
Waving soft coral with fine, feathery polyps. Spreads quickly across rock, so give it room.
Colorful schooling fish that need feeding several times a day. Best for experienced keepers with larger tanks.
c.f: Frozen mysis and brine shrimp, fed several times a day

c.n: Tough, slow plant with dark leaves. Tie to wood or rock and do not bury the rhizome.
Small, colorful dwarf cichlid. Needs caves and plants; males hold territory.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, small pellets

c.n: Bulb plant with wavy leaves that likes a dormant spell. Good midground cover.
General plant entry. Look for the exact species name to see detailed care.
Hardy hawkfish that perches on rocks. Eats small shrimp and very small fish.
Cory with a black stripe that arches from the eye over the back to the tail. Peaceful and best in a group of six.
Shoots water at prey. Needs brackish water and a lid, and will eat small fish.
Eats bristle worms and fireworms. May pick off small fish and shrimp.
c.f: Bristle worms, frozen mysis, meaty foods

c.n: Protected species that is illegal to own in the US. Very large, strong jumper that needs a huge, lidded tank.
Tiny, shy catfish that looks like a stone. Needs a calm nano tank and small live or frozen foods.
c.f: Frozen baby brine shrimp, daphnia, microworms

c.n: Hunts other snails. Use it to control pest snails, but not with snails you want to keep.
Algae-eating snail that grazes rock and glass. Hardy and good for nano tanks.
Caribbean tang that is yellow when young and turns blue as it grows. Needs a large tank and lots of swimming room. Not the same fish as the regal blue tang.
Very aggressive mbuna. Males turn black and gold, females yellow-gold. Best crowded with other mbuna in a large tank.
Active, silvery fish with orange fins. Needs a long tank, neutral to hard water and a group.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Colorful, meaty LPS often sold as a single head. Low to medium light; feed small meaty foods.
Tiny floating fern that turns red in strong light. Spreads fast and shades the tank.
Bright blue and yellow damsel that gets territorial. Best with tough fish.
Hardy, thick stem plant with round leaves. Easy, good for beginners.
Looks small in stores but grows long and needs a large tank in a group of three or more.
Molly bred with a rounded belly and a bent spine. Slower and less hardy than other mollies, so avoid fast tankmates and keep the water clean.
Filter feeder that fans food from the current. Needs good flow and a mature tank.
c.f: Fine particles filtered from the water

c.n: Small lily with banana-shaped roots. Easy; do not bury the roots.
Hardy, active yellow wrasse that jumps. Needs a lid and may eat small ornamental shrimp.
Striking red and white shrimp that sometimes catches small fish. Territorial with others of its own kind.
c.f: Frozen mysis, brine shrimp, fish bits

c.n: Peaceful gourami that stays near the top. Males can squabble with each other, so keep one male with plenty of plants.
Big, active South American fish that eats plants and can bully slow tankmates. Needs a long tank with a tight lid.
Active rainbow with a dark horizontal band that colors up with age. Needs a school and hard, neutral to alkaline water.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Small cory with a dark mask across the eyes. Keep a group of six or more on soft sand or fine gravel.
Peaceful and calm, bred in captivity. Does best in pairs.
Flat, sand-colored catfish that buries itself. Needs soft sand and does not compete well for food.
c.f: Sinking pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Bumpy seahorse that needs a calm, cool tank and frequent frozen meals. Keep only with seahorse-safe tankmates.
Bulb plant with long, wavy leaves that are red below and green-orange above. Prefers soft water.
Tiny blenny that perches in a hole and watches its surroundings. Peaceful and reef-safe, but needs a small hole or empty shell.
Smaller, shy anthias that needs frequent feeding and a group of females.
c.f: Frozen mysis and copepods, fed often

c.n: Delicate black-and-white or red-and-white shrimp that need soft, stable, pure water. Not for beginners.
c.f: Biofilm, powdered shrimp food, algae wafers

c.n: Reef-safe swallowtail angel that eats plankton, not corals. Keep one male, or one male with females.
Quick, hardy danio for larger tanks. Likes a group, open swimming room and a tight lid.
Males flare at their own reflection and fight other males. Likes warm, calm water with plants and slow tank mates.
c.f: Betta pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Dwarf angel with a blue and yellow body. Can nibble corals, and aggressive toward similar angels.
Bold, two-toned blenny that lives in rock holes. May harass small, peaceful fish.
Dark foxface with a yellow face and tail. Venomous spines. Needs a big tank and careful handling.
Long-snouted wrasse that picks at invertebrates and is fast. Needs a lid and a large tank.
Fine-branched SPS that is easier than acropora. Medium to strong light and flow.
Dwarf cichlid with a dark stripe and a blue-yellow body. Keep one male with several females.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, micro pellets

c.n: Dark, almost solid black angelfish. Care is the same as other angelfish. Adults may eat very small fish.
Large, heavy-bodied cichlid with a black belt. Can be aggressive. Needs a big tank.

Hardy, golden tetra that stays calm. Keep six or more.

Fan or branching coral that needs good flow. Photosynthetic types do best.

Surface-living fish that glide above the water. Keep a tight lid, floating plants and calm tank mates.

Pale blue form of a Malawi mbuna. Aggressive toward its own kind.

Tiny cleaner goby that works over rocks. Peaceful and good for nano reefs.

Peaceful wild-type betta that is less flashy than the common betta. Males do not usually fight as hard.
c.f: Frozen daphnia, mosquito larvae, micro pellets

c.n: Hardy, cold-tolerant moss. Tie it to wood or rock. Does well in cooler tanks.
Giant predatory cichlid that can reach over two feet. Only for very large tanks.
c.f: Large pellets, whole shrimp, fish pieces

c.n: Captive-bred clownfish with an almost all white body and orange accents. Same care as ocellaris. Hardy and good for beginners.
Hardy, see-through tetra with a pale yellow glow. Does well in groups of six or more in a planted tank.
Pulsing coral that can grow fast and take over. Easy in some tanks, difficult in others.
Small goby that often lives in a pair with a pistol shrimp. Needs fine sand and a lid, because gobies jump.
c.f: Mysis, brine shrimp, small frozen foods

c.n: Small yellow basslet that often swims upside down under ledges. Peaceful and reef-safe.
Cube-shaped fish that releases toxin when stressed. Juveniles are bright yellow and sold small, but grow large.
Tiny yellow goby that perches on coral. May irritate coral and is sensitive to poor water.
Big wrasse that eats pests but also eats small inverts. Needs sand and a lid.
Bright yellow or orange gorgonian that does not use light. Needs daily feeding of fine foods to survive.
Bright yellow Malawi mbuna, active and territorial. Needs hard alkaline water and rock caves.
Small yellow polyps that spread over rock. Easy, with low to medium light.
Large, hardy seahorse that does best in a quiet tank with slow tankmates. Needs live or frozen foods several times a day.
c.f: Frozen mysis, fed 2 to 3 times a day

c.n: Bright golden neocaridina. Easy to keep in planted tanks with gentle tank mates.
Bright, active algae grazer that needs lots of swimming room. Does not mix well with other tangs of similar shape.
Sand-sifting goby that often pairs with a pistol shrimp. Needs sand and a lid.
Burrowing, mouth-brooding fish that needs deep sand or rubble and a lid. Reef safe.
Tough, boldly colored and territorial. Can harass peaceful tank mates.
Spotted wrasse that buries in sand at night. Needs a lid and a fine sand bed.
Active loach with a pattern that looks like Y-O-Y-O. Needs a group and cover; may eat snails.
Silver angelfish with several dark vertical stripes. Care is the same as other angelfish. Adults may eat very small fish.
Bold, striped fish that is nearly bulletproof. Very active, so give it open water and a tight lid.
Small striped loach, active and social. May eat snails; keep a group.
Barred mbuna in many color forms. Aggressive, best crowded with other mbuna. Needs rocks.
Banded eel with blunt teeth for crushing shells. Ignores most fish but eats crabs and shrimp.
Excellent algae eater. Will not breed in fresh water; needs hard water for its shell.
c.f: Algae and film on glass and rock

c.n: Rare, tiny black-and-white pleco that needs warm, very clean water and caves.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, sinking pellets, some veggies

c.n: Large spiny eel with a zigzag pattern. Eats small fish, needs soft sand and a tight lid.
Colorful, easy coral that grows in colonies. Contains palytoxin, so handle with gloves.
